headline: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute their dismissals in open letter
summary: Three researchers claim OpenAI's communications around their firings may have made colleagues 'afraid to speak,' potentially chilling safety concerns.
details: Three OpenAI safety researchers have penned an open letter disputing their recent dismissals, alleging that the "very public manner" of the company's communications could have a "chilling" effect on employees.

The researchers, Jasmine Wang, Mikita Balesni, and Tomek Korbak, stated they "acted in line with OpenAI's mission and within the working norms of the time." They were reportedly dismissed for sharing information with an external AI safety organization, which OpenAI claims violated policies on accessing sensitive information.

In their letter, the researchers expressed concern that internal and external communications have made former colleagues "afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI." They highlighted that they previously "could raise safety concerns and disagree openly" and were encouraged to consult independent safety organizations.

Addressing other rumors, the researchers denied being the source for a report about OpenAI's new, less monitorable architectures. They also stated that their communication with external parties was done "in coordination and discussion with board members and the C-suite."

The former employees recommended that OpenAI adhere to its public commitments to embed third-party safety auditors, preserve the monitorability of frontier models, and maintain an "open and transparent culture of dialogue between its safety researchers and the rest of the safety ecosystem."

One of the researchers, Jasmine Wang, noted on X that OpenAI leadership "is saying that they strongly agree with our letter," but expressed concern about the company's overall openness and the message sent to current employees about raising concerns.
